title: Even in the Roman School the Protestant way of speaking is owned as Augustinian
source_text: LX. Nec tamen loquendi modus quo utuntur Protestantes, dum aiunt hominem per peccatum amisisse arbitrii libertatem, ad verum & salutare bonum, sic universim in Schola Romana improbatur, quin viri in ea & celebres & docti agnoscant illum ex Augustino desumptum, & scripturae ac veteris Ecclesiae stylo consentaneum esse. Quod bona fide fatentur Jansenius & ejus Discipuli, ut supra a nobis ostensum.
pass_a_gloss: LX. Nor yet is the manner of speaking which the Protestants use, when they say that man through sin has lost the freedom of choice, for true and saving good, so universally disapproved in the Roman School, but that men in it both celebrated and learned acknowledge it to be taken from Augustine, and agreeable to the style of scripture and of the ancient Church. Which Jansenius and his Disciples confess in good faith, as has been shown by us above.
pass_b_english: Yet the Protestant way of speaking, when they say that through sin man lost freedom of choice for true and saving good, is not rejected everywhere in the Roman School: famous and learned men there recognize that it is taken from Augustine and agrees with the language of Scripture and the ancient Church. Jansenius and his disciples admit this honestly, as we showed above.
